//: The tool-calling frameworks `ziffer-scan --code` knows by name (ACP-455). One entry per framework id; `rows` names the row(s) of the coverage table in acp docs/design/acp-455-tool-calling-surfaces.md section 4 (read 2026-09-26) the entry stands for, and every row of that table is named by at least one entry. `packages` are the npm and PyPI names a package.json or a Python manifest declares it by (a trailing `*` matches a prefix: `@scope/*` a whole scope, `@openai/agents-*` a family); `language` is the table's; `covered` is 'milestone-1' when a front end reads its tool definitions, 'not-yet' when the report can only say it is declared. `kind` is 'framework', or 'schema' for a schema library the signatures read (listed so the report can name it, never a tool surface). `CodeTool.sdk` is always one of these ids.
authority_claim_names//: The property names a tool DEFINITION may carry to claim an authority rule (ACP-455, 2026-09-28): each one written on a definition object is reported as `CodeTool.authority_claims`, with its literal value, as a claim the application makes and the draft policy never relies on. `annotations` is an object; the names inside it are read too. `confirmationMessages` is read where a VS Code language model tool's `prepareInvocation` returns it: the editor asks the person first, in its UI only.
confirmation_names//: The names a condition tested before a call to the dispatcher is read as a confirmation check by (ACP-455, 2026-09-28): `CallerCheck.check` is reported when a condition before the call reads a property, an identifier or a string key spelled EXACTLY as one of these. A whole-name match: `confirmedAt` is not `confirmed`.
text_read_calls//: The calls that read a file's text (ACP-460, the third signal): a call to one of these whose first argument (for `Bun.file().text`, the argument of `Bun.file`) resolves from literals, `path.join`/`path.resolve`, `new URL(..., import.meta.url)`, `__dirname`/`import.meta.dirname` to a text file (`.md`, `.mdx`, `.mdc`, `.txt`, `.prompt`) under the scanned root, or to a folder or a one-name pattern holding some, is a `SkillLoad` with `how: 'read'`. A one-word entry matches the called name on any receiver (`fs.readFile`, `fsp.readFile`, `readFile`); a dotted entry must end the callee as written; `X().y` is `y()` called on the result of `X(...)`. A guess may only ADD an inventory entry: nothing here relaxes a grade.
text_glob_calls//: The calls whose result is a list of file paths matched by the glob pattern written as their first argument (ACP-460): a `text_read_calls` read of a loop variable, or of a callback parameter, over one of them resolves to that pattern (`**` any folders, `*` one name).
instruction_params//: The argument properties of a model call (an exposure the front end recognises) that ARE the model's instructions (ACP-460): a loaded text that reaches one of these, or the `content` of a message literal whose `role` is `system` or `developer` in the call's `messages`, is `SkillLoad.reaches.kind: 'instructions'`. One level of nesting is read (`config: { systemInstruction }`).
interception//: Per framework, where a check can stand before its tools run (ACP-455, 2026-09-28; record section 4 table, kinds of section 0): `kind` K1..K5 as `Interception` in src/code/types.ts states them, `name` the place in the framework's own words, as a report may print it. `markers` are the names (an identifier, a property, a keyword argument or a string, whole) whose presence in the code of the file that hands the tools over reads as the hook being registered there, for a front end that has no closer reading of its own; `tool_flags` are the per-tool approval names read on a definition as `CodeTool.interception` (K2). A framework with no entry has no interception point in the table (Instructor: nothing runs).
